problem: VLMs can do high-level task planning but cannot turn reasoning into precise executable actions; they are weak at image-based spatial understanding and pixel-level affordance localization. Prior work also treats object affordance and free-space affordance (where to move or place) independently.
motivation: Embodied navigation and manipulation both need to know how objects can be interacted with and where free space is available for movement or placement. A unified 2D affordance representation grounded in images and lifted to 3D with depth could link language instructions to low-level actions.
key_idea: EspA is an image-to-keypoint hierarchical vision-language model that jointly predicts object affordance and free-space affordance as 2D keypoints from language instructions, then projects them to 3D with depth. It is trained on the new ESA dataset.
insight: Jointly modeling object and free-space affordances in a shared representation space lets the model learn the relation between object functionality and spatial feasibility, which the abstract says gives better spatial understanding than treating them separately. The abstract reports no ablations or numbers, so the evidence for this is not visible here.
method: EspA model: hierarchical vision-language architecture that maps an image plus a language instruction to pixel-level 2D affordance keypoints.
Joint affordance reasoning: object affordance and free-space affordance are predicted in one shared representation space.
2D-to-3D projection: predicted keypoints are lifted to 3D actionable coordinates using depth.
ESA dataset: fine-grained annotations of object-centric interactions and free-space contexts, used for training and as a benchmark.

setting.backbone: Hierarchical vision-language model (EspA); specific base model not stated in the abstract
setting.training_data: ESA (Embodied Spatial Affordance) dataset with object and free-space affordance annotations; scale not given in the abstract
setting.observation: 2D RGB image plus depth (used for 3D projection)
setting.action_space: 2D affordance keypoints projected to 3D coordinates, which are then executed as navigation or manipulation targets

results: According to the abstract, EspA outperforms open-source and closed-source VLMs on object and free-space affordance prediction. It also performs better in real-world navigation and manipulation experiments. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results, baselines and ablations are not visible.
Depends on accurate depth for 3D projection and on single-image keypoint prediction.
